newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU signs trade deal with Palestinian authority.
newsitem.headline: EU signs trade deal with Palestinian authority.

text.p: The European Union and the Palestinian Authority initialled an agreement on Tuesday on full Palestinian partnership in the Euromed accord governing the 15-nation bloc's relations with the Mediterranean region.

The European Commission said the Euro-Mediterranean Interim Association Agreement on Trade and Cooperation "reinforces the message that the EU sees the Palestinians as equal participants in the emerging Euro-Mediterranean space."
An official at the EU executive described it as an important contribution of the Union to the consolidation of the Middle East peace process.

The Euromed accord -- which aims to turn the Mediterranean region into a free-trade zone -- offers lucrative financial incentives to non-EU countries in order to bring their economies into line with the Union.
The deal was initialled by Nabil Sha'ath, Palestinian minister for economic development and planning.
It is similar to other association agreements signed with countries in the region but is adapted to take into account the special status of the Palestinian Authority, the Commission said.
It provides "a wide range of economic and financial cooperation under a programme of support to Palestinian industry."
The agreement confirms trade concessions which the EU has offered the Palestinians since 1986 and provides for free trade within a transitional period of five years.

The EU is the biggest donor of financial aid to Palestinian authorities and since 1993 has contributed over 320 million ecu or European currency units ($397 million) to development of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
This assistance will continue until 1998 with the EU committed to at least 50 million ecu a year in further development grants. (1$=0.80 Ecu)
